cases.root_cause: The IB Gateway became unreachable during pre-open on 2026-10-15. At 09:14:48 the SPX underlying quote was already missing ("no spot price"), and by 09:20 both option and index snapshots hit ConnectionError/TimeoutError as the Gateway API stopped accepting connections — the signature of a Gateway freeze/restart rather than a mere farm blip.

Alpaca answered but delivered bars for ~700 fewer symbols during the 2026-10-15 afternoon window (every intraday run from ~14:00 ET reported missing_bars=700, rows ~3200 vs the 3900 expected), a vendor-side data gap. No runs failed and no bars were quarantined. The gap was not recoverable by the same day's 17:30 eod refetch but was fully recovered by the following day's (2026-10-16 17:30) eod refetch, which returned the full 3900 rows with missing_bars=0.

The IB Gateway's API port was unreachable at 09:10:02 on 2026-10-16, so both the option and index snapshot runs timed out on connect after ~4 seconds (TimeoutError). This was the first collection slot of the day; the gateway was down/restarting (morning login window), and it recovered shortly after — only that single 09:10 slot failed, and every subsequent slot that day succeeded. This matches runbooks/gateway section A ("Task failed: option/index snapshots with TimeoutError() after ~4 s means the connect timed out"), i.e. a transient gateway unavailability, not a full-session freeze.

The IB Gateway's API became unreachable around the market open: the 09:10 pre-open run for both option_snapshots and index_snapshots failed with TimeoutError() after ~4s (API port not accepting connections), and no snapshots landed between ~09:50 and 10:41 while the Gateway was down/reconnecting. It then recovered (option coverage was 100%, 78/78), but the recovery pushed subsequent slots late (on-time only 60.26%), which is why many morning runs ran late.

The 10:09:43 equity_bars run failed with RemoteProtocolError('Server disconnected without sending a response.') — a transient Alpaca API connection drop. It was a single isolated failure: every subsequent equity_bars run that day succeeded with missing_bars=0, and no other datasets were affected, so no data was lost and no action is needed.

The 09:20 option snapshot run hung on an IBKR request and was killed by its 8-minute execution timeout (duration 480s exactly) with every chain failing before any rows were written, so no error was recorded. This is the same signature as the contract-definition/secdef stall in incidents/2026-10-23 — a slow upstream IBKR service held up the run until the budget was exhausted. It was transient: the next slot succeeded and the day's coverage is 78/78, so no data was ultimately lost.

The recurring 10090/10167/354 IBKR codes on option snapshot runs indicate a market-data subscription/permission problem for the collector user: code 10090/354 means "not subscribed for this instrument", and 10167 means "delayed data shown instead of live". These are not connection/farm issues and self-healing (RECONNECTDATA/RESTART) does not run for them — a restart cannot fix a subscription.

The 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23 option snapshots were NOT lost. Those sessions ran on the Mac host (collection moved to the Windows host ~2026-10-27), so their run records don't exist in this host's pipeline_runs — get_runs returns "no runs recorded" for both days. This host's slo_status therefore reads option_ok=0 (0% coverage) for those two days, a monitoring artifact, not a data loss.

IBKR's contract-definition (secdef) server stopped answering for ~5 minutes starting at 10:35 ET, and because every option/index run made contract-definition requests (qualifyContracts, reqSecDefOptParams) before streaming quotes, the stalled requests hung the runs.

The 08:15 contract_cache refresh overloaded IBKR's contract-definition (secdef) service (~24 MB across ~23k messages while re-listing ~55 expiries); the market-data farm broke (2103) and secdef stopped answering, and by ~09:16 ET the IB Gateway's API port stopped accepting connections entirely. The Gateway froze for the rest of the session, so all regular-hours option snapshot runs failed, and its self-healing never fired because check_gateway only caught connect errors, not a request that hung after connecting.

Both 09:10 failures on 2026-10-27 and 2026-10-30 are the same cause: the IB Gateway's API port was not accepting connections at the market open, so the option and index snapshot tasks failed their connect with `TimeoutError()` after ~4 seconds. This is the "Gateway API unreachable" pattern (gateway.md section A), the same root-cause as the 2026-10-26 freeze that recurred each morning until commit ef762db.

A routine, self-recovered IBKR connectivity/farm blip. Codes 1100 followed by 1102 ("data maintained") and 2103 followed by 2110 (farm reconnect) recovered within the same session — no data was lost and no action is needed.

These are routine, self-recovering IBKR market-data farm drops, not a Gateway failure. Codes 2103/2157 appear roughly daily on specific runs, but every run still succeeds with full row counts and no data is lost: SLI 1 (option coverage) is 100% for every recent session (10-27 onward) and SLI 3 (bars) is 100%. Per runbooks/gateway section D, farm drops that recover within the same run (2103→2104) and daily farm drops are routine and not alerted; no action is needed.

The IBKR market-data connection went down before/around the open, so the 09:10–09:25 option/index snapshot slots had no earlier successful run all morning (the last success was the prior day's 15:55 close, ~17.4h gap). The queued slots fired in a burst once the Gateway briefly responded around 09:25, but the connection was still broken: three failed with TimeoutError() after ~4s (API connect timeout) and one with "Socket disconnect / Not connected" across every chain carrying farm codes 2104/2106/2119/2158.

The data volume is out of disk space. Every run since 13:05 ET on 2026-11-12 across all datasets (option_snapshots, index_snapshots, equity_bars, daily_bars, corporate_actions, assets) fails in ~2 seconds with OSError(28, 'No space left on device'). The last successful run was option_snapshots at 13:00 ET (284s, 3817 rows), after which no run has succeeded.

The eod.dbt_build task failed because another process (a Python 3.12 process, PID 4127) holds an open handle on data/curated.duckdb, so DuckDB refused the write lock. Collection is not affected: every collection run on 2026-11-12 succeeded, since collectors write raw/staged Parquet, not through DuckDB.

Alpaca API is rejecting the collector with HTTP 401 Unauthorized on https://data.alpaca.markets/v2/stocks/bars, so every equity_bars run fails immediately (1s duration, all 90 runs) and no bars are staged for 2026-11-12. This is a vendor (Alpaca) auth/credential failure, not an IB Gateway problem — option snapshots continue to collect fine from IBKR.

IBKR error code 10197 ("live data held by another session of the same user") on every option snapshot run for 2026-11-12. Another TWS/mobile/web session using the same collector username is holding the live market-data session, so requests complete successfully but return no quotes (no_quote=3400, two_sided=0 in every run). This is a subscription issue, not a Gateway fault — the Gateway is healthy and runs succeed.

The host, Docker or Airflow was down for the entire 2026-11-12 session (and still down through 2026-11-13). No runs were recorded at all — not failed runs, but zero slots — which rules out a Gateway/IBKR data issue and points to the collection stack not running.

The 08:15 contract_cache refresh overloaded IBKR's contract-definition (secdef) service again, causing the 08:20 Gateway check to report "❌ 合约查询" (secdef requests didn't answer within 20 s). The stall left a hung request that consumed each pre-open option-snapshot run's whole 6-minute budget (TimeoutError + "skipped: run budget used up") and killed the index-snapshot runs, from 09:10 through ~09:25. It self-cleared during the session: from 15:00 onward option/index snapshots succeeded normally with no IBKR error codes, so the Gateway itself was not wedged and no farm/subscription problem was involved.

Six consecutive option_snapshot runs (11:00–11:25 ET) each consumed their full 8-minute (480s) execution timeout and were killed with no error recorded — the signature of a single IBKR request hanging for the whole run budget. The failure was isolated to option snapshots: index_snapshots and equity_bars had zero failures and equity bars were 100% complete, so the Gateway and Alpaca were otherwise healthy; a specific option-chain request hung until the execution timeout killed each run.

IBKR market-data farms disconnected (codes 2103/2105) during 13:00–13:25 ET, causing every option snapshot run to fail with "SPX: no spot price". Each run already sent RECONNECTDATA, which returned OK, but the farms did not recover within the window, so the underlying spot price remained unavailable.

The IB Gateway was stuck waiting for second-factor authentication (phone push) from 08:58 until 10:17, so its API port was not accepting connections and every option/index snapshot from 09:10 to 10:15 timed out with TimeoutError() after ~4 s. The login completed at 10:17 and collection resumed normally.

Alpaca has no bars for a ~45-minute window on 2026-11-12 (≈9 five-minute slots × 50 symbols = 450 bars), and the 17:30 eod refetch already ran without recovering them, so the gap is on Alpaca's side and currently not re-fetchable.

A transient IBKR connectivity blip at ~11:00 ET (code 1100, restored shortly after by 1102 "data maintained", same session) caused one in-flight option snapshot request to hang and hit its 300s RequestTimeout, failing the 11:00 run with TimeoutError(). The failure held the single run slot for the full 5 minutes, so the subsequent slots (11:05–11:30) started late under max_active_runs=1. The Gateway itself stayed connected throughout.
